issues.legal_issue: A statutory cess provision tied to a valuation under another enactment remains operative when the existing assessment book used for that valuation has been invalidated.
material_facts: The cess on urban lands and buildings was calculated as a percentage of annual letting value determined under the municipal law.
The assessment book then used to determine annual letting value had been invalidated because it used a flat floor-area method and included plant and machinery.
No current annual letting value was available, but the valuation could be revised or new valuation principles established.
issues.conclusion: The invalidation of the assessment book did not invalidate the cess provision; it remained on the statute book and could be applied to a revised assessment book or valuation.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12 of the Gujarat Education Cess Act, 1962, imposed the tax by reference to annual letting value determined under the Bombay Provincial Municipal Corporations Act, 1949. The invalidity of the existing assessment book did not make section 12 fail: the provision could operate on a later valid valuation. The Court relied on its decision in New Manek Chowk Spinning & Weaving Co. Ltd. v. Municipal Corporation of the City of Ahmedabad, which had invalidated the assessment method.

predicates.cess_is_calculated_from_an_external_prop: The law calculates a cess as a percentage of a property valuation determined through a separate assessment process.
predicates.existing_valuation_method_was_invalidate: A court invalidated the valuation method then being used in the separate assessment process.
predicates.replacement_valuation_can_be_prepared: A valid replacement assessment or valuation can be prepared.
predicates.new_valuation_principles_can_be_set: The relevant lawmaking authority can establish principles for a new valuation.

issues.definition: When a cess depends on an external property valuation, invalidation of the existing valuation method does not prevent the cess provision from operating if a replacement valuation or new valuation principles can be provided.

issues.legal_issue: Different methods of imposing a cess on properties in different zones do not, without proof of a heavier burden, establish unconstitutional discrimination.
material_facts: Properties in one zone bore only a tax on lands and buildings, properties in another bore only a surcharge on land revenue, and properties in the middle zone bore both a surcharge and a tax.
The middle-zone properties had been diverted from agricultural use and were also within municipal limits, while properties in the other zones had different land-use and tax characteristics.

The property valuation method had been invalidated, and the petitioners did not establish that the middle zone's combined burden was heavier than the single levy in the other zones apart from relying on that invalid method.
The rates could be adjusted to account for the advantages associated with the cess and the locations of the lands.
issues.conclusion: The different methods of calculation and the fact of double imposition in the middle zone did not, by themselves, establish discrimination under Article 14; no discriminatory heavier burden had been shown.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 of the Constitution prohibits unequal treatment, but a double imposition in one zone is not by itself discriminatory when compared with a single levy in other zones. Discrimination requires showing that the combined levy falls more heavily; different methods of calculation alone are insufficient. The Court also considered that rates could be adjusted equitably in light of the advantages derived from the cess and the lands' locations. It relied on the earlier decision invalidating the flat-rate floor-area valuation method, which was expected to lead to a revised assessment.

rule.if: constitutional_equality_challenge_to_zone_based_cess and zones_have_different_levy_methods and one_zone_has_multiple_levies and not heavier_comparative_burden_shown

predicates.constitutional_equality_challenge_to_zon: A taxpayer challenges a zone-based cess on the ground that it treats property holders unequally.
predicates.zones_have_different_levy_methods: Property holders in different zones are charged through different levy methods.
predicates.one_zone_has_multiple_levies: Property holders in one zone are subject to more than one levy while those in other zones are subject to a single levy.
predicates.heavier_comparative_burden_shown: Evidence establishes that the combined levy in one zone falls more heavily than the single levy in other zones.

issues.definition: In a zone-based equality challenge, different levy methods and multiple levies in one zone do not establish discrimination when no heavier comparative burden is shown.

issues.legal_issue: A cess calculated as an addition to an existing tax does not require a separate assessment procedure or separate opportunity to object when the underlying assessment process provides scrutiny and appeals.
material_facts: The cess was calculated as a percentage of a tax assessed under other legislation rather than through an independent assessment.
The underlying assessment processes allowed taxpayers to raise objections and provided for appeals.
The petitioners challenged the absence of a separate procedure under the cess law for objections, representations, or appeals.
issues.conclusion: The absence of a separate assessment procedure and opportunity for objections or appeals under the cess law did not violate natural justice or invalidate the law.
issues.legal_principle: The cess was an arithmetical addition to an assessment made under other legislation. Where the underlying assessment process allows objections and appeals, a further opportunity to challenge the calculation of the percentage-based cess is unnecessary. A cess law need not be self-contained as to assessment; incorporation of and reference to another legislative scheme is an effective and constitutional method of imposing, levying, and collecting a cess.

predicates.validity_challenge_to_percentage_based_c: A taxpayer challenges the validity of a cess calculated as a percentage of an existing tax.
predicates.cess_uses_underlying_tax_assessment: The cess calculation uses the result of an assessment made under a separate tax scheme rather than an independent assessment.
predicates.underlying_process_allows_objections_and: The separate tax assessment process permits objections and provides for appeals.

issues.definition: A percentage-based cess using an underlying tax assessment does not require a separate assessment procedure when that underlying process permits objections and appeals.
